correctness.rationale: All quantified hypotheses are real B>0, 0<q<16, five independent nonnegative conductances. Exact 5x5 Laplacian eigenvectors and reflection blocks have eigenvalue 1 and the remaining nonzero eigenvalues exceed 1; Q(a) is strictly decreasing from 16 to 0 because its degree-six derivative numerator has seven negative Bernstein coefficients on the larger interval [3/5,4/5]. Positive alpha,beta give exact edgewise dual identities equal to all five individual prices, hence a global upper bound for arbitrary asymmetric allocations. Equality forces both two Fiedler eigenvectors and uniquely all five weights. Exact polynomial algebra was independently replayed with SymPy from verify.py, plus 1520 supplemental finite numerical checks; finite checks are not the infinite-parameter proof.

value.rationale: A natural one-exceptional-price five-cycle, the first nontrivial odd cycle beyond a triangle, is a canonical network-resource design instance where two distinct low symmetry modes compete. The old q=16 edge-retention boundary leaves a genuine open strictly active interval. The theorem obtains the entire 0<q<16 unique global independent-conductance optimum by exact inverse algebra, nontrivial Bernstein monotonicity, and a rank-two dual eigenvector certificate. It quantifies optimal mixing with explicit rational witnesses and limiting values, rather than arbitrarily tabulating small cases or restating SDP solvability.
